guard: Implicit foreground actors allocate without replacing held material, while explicit identities and non-collision failures remain pinned
why: The real-process suite uses fail-fast assertions with dependent lifecycle steps. A named assertion failure intentionally stops later steps, while finally reaps every owned process. Do not require the success-only completion line on an expected red.

mutations.name: disable implicit foreground collision allocation
mutations.find: if (!autoName || !(e instanceof ForegroundActorCollision || e instanceof AgentGrantConflictError || e instanceof AgentAlreadyRunning)) throw e;
mutations.replace: if (!autoName || process.pid > 0 || !(e instanceof ForegroundActorCollision || e instanceof AgentGrantConflictError || e instanceof AgentAlreadyRunning)) throw e;
mutations.expectRed: implicit foreground launch allocates a fresh actor while prior material is held

mutations.name: ignore an explicit actor pin on collision
mutations.find: if (!autoName || !(e instanceof ForegroundActorCollision || e instanceof AgentGrantConflictError || e instanceof AgentAlreadyRunning)) throw e;
mutations.replace: if (!(e instanceof ForegroundActorCollision || e instanceof AgentGrantConflictError || e instanceof AgentAlreadyRunning)) throw e;
mutations.expectRed: explicit held identity never launches a replacement

mutations.name: treat an ordinary authorization failure as name occupancy
mutations.find: if (!autoName || !(e instanceof ForegroundActorCollision || e instanceof AgentGrantConflictError || e instanceof AgentAlreadyRunning)) throw e;

mutations.name: refuse an implicit launch instead of skipping an existing remote grant
mutations.replace: if (process.pid < 0 && checked.exists && "provisioningUrl" in source) throw new ForegroundActorCollision(checked.message);
mutations.expectRed: implicit launch skips an existing remote grant as well as a local held name
